questions.stem: Arjan Steel exports Rs 600 crore of goods billed in USD (receivable in 90 days) and imports Rs 400 crore (payable in 90 days); a subsidiary's net assets (USD) translate on consolidation; the CFO must choose the hedging architecture.

questions.q: The rupee depreciates to 86 from 83 at the horizon; unhedged on the net 200 Cr position, the P&L gain approx:
questions.why: Net INR gain = 200×(86/83 −1) ≈ Rs 7.23 crore — the residual exposure is what the hedge or its absence creates.

questions.q: Translation exposure on the sub's USD net assets:
o: Reduce by funding-in-currency (USD debt) or treat as accounting-only volatility; hedge of OCI is not cost-effective for long-term
questions.why: Long-term translation exposure is best managed structurally (borrow in the sub's currency to match); derivative-hedging an OCI number can create cash-flow risk (Ind AS 109 permits a net-investment hedge in principle, but covering a pencil number with cash is rarely the standard answer).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).

mem.tip: Translation: fix the structure, not the rate Don't pay cash to hedge a pencil number — move the pencil.

questions.q: For receivables awaiting tender awards (not yet firm contracts), the right instrument is:
o: FX put options (buy the right when the order wins)
questions.why: Contingent exposures ⇒ options: no obligation if the tender is lost; forwards would leave an uncovered short USD — speculation by backfire.

questions.q: A receivable in USD due 90 days, with a 90-day forward quote available; hedging via forward converts:
o: The uncertain future spot into a certain rupee amount (transaction exposure)
questions.why: Forward cover removes the variability of the future conversion rate — the classic transaction exposure hedge; translation risk remains on foreign operations.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — exposure-taxonomy with instruments matching is the forex chapter's core Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: A forward locks the rate; the only remaining fear is that the deal itself dies.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

questions.q: An exporter expecting USD in 90 days, with expected INR appreciation, should consider:
o: Convert at maturity only — no timing shift
Buy USD forwards to lengthen exposure
questions.why: INR expected to APPRECIATE means USD expected to weaken: collect the USD receivable EARLY (lead) and defer foreign-currency payments (lag) — take the weakening currency sooner and hand it over later.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the leads/lags direction question with expectation overhangs AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Ride the expected drop: grab the weaker money sooner, hand over the stronger later.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

questions.q: Which exposure is affected by restating foreign subsidiary accounts into reporting currency?
questions.why: Translation exposure = accounting effect of re-measurement (current rate/temporal methods) on consolidated equity — no cash flow impact per se; economic exposure = long-run cash flow shift.

mem.tip: Translation moves the pencil in equity; transaction moves the cash; economic moves the business.

questions.q: Which instrument swaps fixed interest obligations between counterparties?
questions.why: Plain vanilla IRS: one party pays fixed, one pays floating on a notional; FRA is 1-period rate lock; basis swaps floating-vs-floating different index.

questions.q: Buying a currency call instead of a forward is justified when:
o: The entity wants protection but also the benefit of favourable movements (option value premium)
questions.why: Option = insurance with premium; forward = lock that forfeits the favourable tail; expected-value trade-off and premium affordability decide.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — insurance-vs-lock reasoning AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A forward deletes the surprise; an option keeps the good one and charges for it.

questions.q: Bilateral netting of FX payables/receivables among group entities reduces exposure by:
o: Offsetting only the matched currencies/tenors; residual net flows hedged — cuts transaction costs and exposure on offset amounts
questions.why: Netting settles differences — saves gross flows but residual mismatch (currency/tenor) still needs cover; multi-currency netting via clearing centre for group structures.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — netting-benefit-and-limits phrasing AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Cancel what offsets; hedge what remains.

questions.q: Exporter (USD 200 lakh) can forward-cover at 84.20 or stay open; year-end spot may be 85.50 or 82.00. The correct EXPOSURE trade-off statement is:
o: Hedging gains vs spot-82 scenario by Rs 4.40 lakh, costs that much if spot ends at 85.5 (certainty traded for upside)
questions.why: Forward locks 168.4 lakh; open: 171.0 (better by 2.6 lakh) or 164.0 (worse by 4.4 lakh). Hedging removes BOTH outcomes — that is the trade, not a bet on direction.

questions.q: A US subsidiary of an Indian parent operates independently in USD (functional currency). On consolidation the translation differences on its net assets go:
o: Self-sustaining foreign sub: current rate method — translation gain/loss to OCI until disposal
questions.why: Ind AS 21: functional = foreign currency ⇒ current-rate method: all items closing rate, income avg; exchange differences to OCI (CTDR) and recycled on disposal. If integral to parent (temporal): monetary closing, non-monetary historical, differences to P&L.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — functional-currency test driving the method and the destination is the translation exam AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Current rate for self-sufficient sub: equity/retained differences to OCI; temporal for integral: to P&L.
